Caroline / Jasmine — quick technical note to supplement the MAP: 

- For secure payments workloads we recommend starting on Hosted with customer‑scoped keys (bring‑your‑own‑KMS) and explicit audit‑log forwarding to your SIEM. Hosted gives fastest time to evaluate features and reduces initial procurement friction.
- Dedicated should be considered if you need data plane isolation and predictable throughput. Typical lift for Dedicated: 1–2 weeks to provision, plus additional network peering (2–3 days) for private connectivity.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem) is the only choice if you require full air‑gapped policies or an HSM integrated into your on‑prem stack — that path typically adds 3–6 weeks for security review and network validation.

I’ll include a lightweight test plan in the MAP: workload profile, sequence lengths, SLOs we’ll measure, and a minimal set of prompts to validate correctness.

— Karthik

Caroline — attaching the commercial term summary you requested and a sensitivity table that compares Hosted vs Dedicated at three volume scenarios (low / expected / high). High level takeaways: 

- At your expected volume (we used the token estimates you provided last week), Dedicated (6‑month commit) comes in ~12% cheaper than Hosted with moderate burst allowance; with a larger throughput requirement Dedicated savings increase.
- Hosted removes operational burden and accelerates time to PoC (same day provisioning), Dedicated gives performance predictability and cost savings at scale.
- Private (VPC) adds a platform onboarding fee and per‑month networking cost; we estimated network peering + KMS setup adds one‑time ~$12k engineering onboarding for your environment.

I’ve uploaded the term sheet and sensitivity table to the Drive link in the MAP and added notes for procurement redlines we typically see (data processing addendum, KMS clauses, SLA uptime language).

If procurement wants a canned quote for procurement review I can generate a formal quote by EOD Friday (6/19).
